_note: The sensitivity ladder, ordered least to most sensitive. Each description is handed to Jev verbatim as the criteria for that class, so editing a description IS editing the decision. Keep them about what the content contains -- personal data, credentials -- and never about who is allowed to receive it: this module does not know about vendors, models or approvals.
instructions: Classify the sensitivity of this content by what it actually contains. Judge the content itself, not the topic it discusses: text that merely mentions passwords is not a credential, and a sentence about a patient is not a medical record. When content matches more than one class, choose the most sensitive one that genuinely applies.

classes.description: Nothing that identifies a person and nothing that grants access. Published documentation, open-source code, marketing copy, generic questions. Releasing it costs nothing.

No personal data and no credentials, but not for outsiders: unreleased plans, internal process, private source code, architecture and infrastructure detail, pricing and commercial terms. A leak is a business loss, not a loss to any individual.

Identifies a specific living person, or grants access to a system. Names with contact details, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, user accounts and IDs, IP addresses, employee or customer records. Also secrets: API keys, access tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings, session cookies.

Personal data a statute protects, or a credential that moves money or reaches production. National ID and passport numbers, bank and payment card numbers, health and medical records, biometrics, precise location history, data about children, and special-category data such as race, religion, politics, union membership, sexual orientation or criminal record. Also long-lived production credentials.
